task.title: Reuse content with conref and conkeyref
task.shortdesc: Write a note, step or paragraph once in a chunks file and pull it into any topic. The build inlines it, and every page that uses it updates together.

step.cmd: Put reusable elements, each with an id, in a topic under reuse/.

stepxmp.codeblock: <topic id="common"> <title>Reusable content</title> <body> <note id="restart" type="note">Restart the web service and the worker after changing a variable.</note> <steps> <step id="step-build"><cmd>Build the packages: <codeph>pnpm build</codeph>.</cmd></step> </steps> </body> </topic>

info.p: Leave the file out of every map. A chunks file is not published on its own, and validation does not warn about it as long as some published topic uses one of its chunks.

step.cmd: Pull a chunk in with conref, using the path, the topic id and the element id.
Or define a key for the chunks file once, and use conkeyref so topics need no relative paths.

stepxmp.codeblock:
<!-- in a map --> <keydef keys="reuse" href="../reuse/common.dita"/>
<!-- in any topic --> <step conkeyref="reuse/step-build"/>

info.p: This page itself pulls its restart note in with conkeyref:

ul.li: References work within a file and across files, and chunks may reference other chunks. Cycles are reported as conref-cycle.

The referencing element should have the same name as the chunk. A

that pulls a works but warns (conref-type-mismatch).

Filtering attributes on the referencing element apply to the pulled content, so <note conkeyref="reuse/restart" product="core"/> shows the shared note to core readers only. Attributes on the chunk itself apply too.
Keys inside a chunk resolve in the keyspace of the map publishing the topic that pulls it.
conrefend and conaction are not supported: only the start element is pulled, with a warning.

result.p: The release snapshot records which topics use each chunk, so tools can show the impact of changing one.
